paragraphs: Debe. You will often find debe and bidve in the Talmud. 1) Bidve Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai. Rashi explains, chapter Passin, 19a: a baraita arranged in his study house. (See Rabbah bar Maryon.) 2) Debe bar Maryon (see his entry). 3) Zuti of the house of Rav Pappi. 4) Rabbi Yitzchak of the house of Rabbi Ammi. 5) A reciter of the house of Rabbi Ammi: Berakhot 14a; that is, one student who recited in Rabbi Ammi’s house. 6) Ashyan, a reciter of the house of Rabbi Ammi. 7) Rabbi Yitzchak of the house of Rabbi Yannai. 8) The house of Rabbi Yannai: Chelek, 98, end of side b, and 102. 9) The house of Shmuel; see his entry. 10) Achi, a reciter of the house of Rabbi Chiyya, who recited in Rabbi Chiyya’s house: Berakhot 14. 11) In the house of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov: Sanhedrin 92b; Chullin 132a. See Rabbi Chanina bar Minyomi. 12) Mar Yehudah of the house of Mar Yochani. 13) It raises an objection from Rabbi Yishmael against what the house of Rabbi Yishmael recites; see his entry. 14) “Debe and Menashe” [דבי ומנשה]. 15) The house of Rav said: Chelek, 96a. 16) The house of Rabbi Sheila say: there, and folio 108; see there. 17) The house of Rabbi Chanina: there, 98, end of side b. 18) The house of Levi: see Rabbi Shemayah bar Zeira. 19) The house of Rabbi Acha: see Shimon bar Zevid. 20) A reciter of the house of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon: Sotah 11a. 21) In Nazir 43b: “Rav Kahana recited in the house of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov”—this is how it should read. 22) Wherever there is “Rav Safra teaches in the name of one of Rabbi’s house,” it means the distinguished one among his sons; who is that? Rabban Gamliel. In a gloss to Maimonides’ introduction to order Zeraim (see Rav Safra).
